subject: Re: Redwood Inference demo — next steps + sample requests
body:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@harborviewpayments.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@harborviewpayments.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Redwood Inference demo — next steps + sample requests

Megan (and Tom) — thanks again for the time yesterday.

Sharing a quick recap + a proposed mutual action plan so we can keep momentum.

Demo recap (what we covered)
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options (and what typically triggers each)
- Console views for latency + token cost breakdown; tracing hooks
- How we handle bursty workloads (batching/caching + routing policies)
- What “Dedicated” gives you: isolated capacity + predictable throughput
- What “Private” gives you: customer-managed networking boundaries + audit-ready controls (VPC/on-prem patterns)

Proposed mutual action plan (2-week eval)
1) Harborview sends:
   - 2–3 representative request payloads + typical max prompt/context lengths
   - Target throughput + latency SLO (p50/p95) by route if you have it
   - Any hard requirements on VPC-only / private connectivity vs. public API
2) Redwood sends:
   - A test endpoint + model options aligned to your use case
   - A recommended configuration (streaming vs non-streaming, batching/caching knobs)
   - Security answers on retention, audit logs, KMS options for Dedicated/Private
3) Working sessions:
   - 45 min technical deep dive (platform team + our SE) to size capacity + integration plan
   - 30 min security/GRC Q&A (retention, logging, data handling boundaries)
4) Decision checkpoint:
   - End of week 2: go/no-go on a scoped POC and whether Dedicated vs Private is the right path

Two quick questions from my side:
- What’s your preferred auth model for eval (IP allowlist + API key, or SSO later)?
- Do you expect production traffic to require private connectivity from day one, or is that a phase 2 requirement?

Attaching a 1-page recap for internal sharing.

If it helps, I can also get you a short sample curl payload + response format for your team to validate the integration flow.

Best,
Priyom

Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwoodinference.com

Priyom — thanks for the recap.

Two asks from our side:
1) Can you share 1–2 example request payloads (chat/generation) that reflect what you’d consider a “best practice” structure? We’ll map them to our internal gateway.
2) We need clarity on data retention. Specifically:
   - Do you store prompts/outputs by default?
   - How long are logs retained (and what’s in them)?
   - Can we configure retention / disable storage?

On private connectivity: we strongly prefer VPC-only in production, but we can start with a public endpoint for eval if security is comfortable with the posture.

Thanks,
Megan

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@harborviewpayments.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@harborviewpayments.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Redwood Inference demo — next steps + sample requests

Megan — totally makes sense.

(1) Sample payloads
Below are two representative examples your team can use to wire up the gateway. If you share your expected schema constraints (headers, idempotency keys, etc.), we can mirror those.

Example A — chat (streaming)
POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers:
- Authorization: Bearer <api_key>
- Content-Type: application/json
Body:
{
  "model": "redwood/verified-<model_name>",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a compliance-aware assistant. Provide concise, auditable answers."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the following customer message and flag potential fraud indicators: ..."}
  ],
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "max_tokens": 400,
  "stream": true
}

Example B — text generation (non-streaming)
POST /v1/completions
Body:
{
  "model": "redwood/verified-<model_name>",
  "prompt": "Classify the following transaction narrative into one of [A, B, C] and explain why: ...",
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "max_tokens": 200,
  "stop": ["\n\n"]
}

If you’d prefer, we can also provide a minimal Postman collection (just say the word).

(2) Retention (high level; Aisha can provide the approved language)
At a high level, we separate:
- Request/response content (prompts/outputs)
- Operational telemetry (metrics, limited request metadata)
- Audit events (access/config changes)

We can support a “public endpoint for eval” as long as we align on what’s permitted for that phase (e.g., synthetic data only vs. limited real traffic) and what security posture you need.

Aisha (CISO) is CC’d and can confirm the exact wording we should use for your internal security review.

Next step proposal
- Can we do a 30 min security Q&A tomorrow or Friday? Markus can also join if your platform folks want to discuss VPC-only architecture options.

Priyom

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood Inference demo — next steps + sample requests

Megan — jumping in on retention with the security-approved framing.

Prompts/outputs
- Redwood’s default posture for our hosted API is to process prompts/outputs to generate responses and not use your content to train models.
- For regulated workloads, we typically recommend Dedicated or Private depending on your network/isolation requirements.

Logging and retention (what you can expect to see)
- Operational logging is designed to support reliability/security monitoring (e.g., timestamps, model/route identifiers, request IDs, error codes, latency). We avoid including full prompt/output content in standard operational logs.
- Audit events (e.g., user access changes, key configuration changes) are available for review and can be exported for compliance workflows.

Configuration / controls
- Retention and export requirements vary by deployment mode. In Private deployments (VPC / on-prem patterns), customers can keep sensitive content and logs within their controlled environment and align retention to internal policy.
- For an evaluation on a public endpoint, we can align on a safe testing approach (commonly: synthetic or pre-approved data) while we concurrently validate the Dedicated/Private architecture.

I’m attaching a short overview we use for security review calls (non-confidential). If you need more detailed evidence, we can coordinate under NDA.

Happy to join a 30-min security Q&A.

Regards,
Aisha

Dr. Aisha Rahman
Chief Information Security Officer
